note: Structured record of what was decided, built and verified. Observable facts and short decision rationales only — never reasoning traces, private prompts, credentials or customer data. Unknown values stay null rather than being guessed.

events.goal: Establish what the environment can actually do before committing to an architecture.
events.decision_summary: Verified toolchain, GitHub identity and scopes, Cloudflare account and token permissions, disk space, and that verify.itisyou.app was unclaimed.
alternatives_considered: Assume the documented environment and start building
events.decision_reason: The plan explicitly warns against assuming account access. Three findings changed later decisions: the Cloudflare OAuth token carries zone:read only, the account already holds 32 unrelated Workers and 13 unrelated D1 databases, and this machine's local DNS resolver is broken so hostname checks must use DNS-over-HTTPS.
events.limitations: Cloudflare plan tier was inferred from the existing count of 13 D1 databases exceeding the free-tier limit, not read from a billing API.
events.next_step: Freeze the shared contracts before delegating.

events.goal: Freeze the vocabulary every agent shares, so twelve specialists cannot each invent their own.
events.decision_summary: The customer rule language is a closed set of typed operators over an allowlisted set of fields. Money is integer minor units with a single budget-availability formula.
alternatives_considered: A general expression language (JSONLogic, CEL, a sandboxed JS subset)
Decimal money library
events.decision_reason: A general expression language would let a customer rule become an unbounded computation or a network request, and would make the FAILED/UNVERIFIED distinction unprovable. Integer pence removes an entire class of cap-drift bug; a decimal library would add a dependency for no benefit at this scale.
test_evidence_refs: tsc strict clean
events.limitations: The operator set covers the one supported workflow shape. A second workflow shape will need a contract version bump, not an added escape hatch.

events.goal: Prove the hosting path end to end before building on it.
events.decision_summary: Two D1 databases in EU-West, staging and production Workers, custom domain verify.itisyou.app, cron on production only. Background work uses a D1 due-job table plus a one-minute cron trigger rather than Cloudflare Queues.
alternatives_considered: Cloudflare Queues for background work
Durable Object ledger for budget accounting
Default ENAM database region
events.decision_reason: A D1 due-job table with a partial index is deterministic, testable without network, and adds no dependency; Queues would add delivery semantics we would then have to test around. EU-West was chosen over the default ENAM for a UK business. Staging deliberately has no cron so a test environment cannot generate recurring cost.
test_evidence_refs: 0001_init.sql applied to both remote databases: 70 statements each
https://verify.itisyou.app returns 200 with valid TLS
/health probes D1 and reports database reachable
events.limitations: The site currently serves an honest holding page. Nothing is for sale and no account can be created.

events.goal: Make a permanently public repository safe before any code that touches credentials exists.
events.decision_summary: Secret scanning and push protection enabled, private vulnerability reporting enabled, Dependabot alerts and its automatic dependency-update pull requests enabled, a branch ruleset blocking deletion and force-push and requiring a reviewed pull request, and default workflow permissions set to read.
alternatives_considered: Start private and flip to public at release
events.decision_reason: The founder requires permanent public visibility, so every byte must be treated as permanently disclosed from the first commit. Writing .gitignore and the secret scanner before generating any credential is the only ordering that works.
test_evidence_refs: GitHub push protection blocked a push containing credential-shaped test fixtures; fixtures were rewritten rather than allowlisted
events.limitations: Repository-admin bypass on the ruleset is deliberate so the owner can push directly. External contributions require review.

events.goal: Settle the offer and write factual copy, so no agent later invents a claim.
events.decision_summary: Produced a claims-to-implementation map and cut every claim nothing implements.
events.decision_reason: Claims cut included real-time results (results depend on a one-minute poll and a deadline up to an hour), works with any CRM, we tell you the automation is broken (we observe downstream evidence, not the automation), and tenant isolation stated as a present-tense guarantee before the enforcing code existed.
test_evidence_refs: tsc strict clean
events.limitations: Legal identity fields left as TODO_OWNER_INPUT. Worst-case external-call volume of 4,000 per workspace per month is an estimate pending the connector implementation.

events.goal: Make a false VERIFIED structurally impossible.
events.decision_summary: Pure, time-injected evaluator and decision table. Email normalisation deliberately does not strip +tags or dots. Only RECORD_NOT_FOUND and EVENT_NOT_OBSERVED are authoritative absences.
alternatives_considered: Gmail-style email normalisation
Treating any missing evidence at the deadline as FAILED
events.decision_reason: Verification must never widen an equivalence class: stripping a +tag would let an address the customer controls satisfy a rule about emailing the enquirer. Treating any absence as FAILED would convert our own outages into customer failures.
test_evidence_refs: 195 cases VERIFY-001..VERIFY-195, all passing
events.limitations: Pure logic only. It proves the decision is correct given a bundle; it does not prove the bundle was gathered correctly — that is A04's connectors.
events.next_step: Connectors must supply provider_account_id and honest origin values.

events.goal: Tenant scoping, idempotency and credential handling that hold under concurrency.
events.decision_summary: AES-GCM credential envelopes bind workspace, provider and purpose into the AAD. Source-event admission reserves the run allowance inside the same D1 batch using a CASE expression that violates NOT NULL on exhaustion, forcing a rollback.
alternatives_considered: Conditional UPDATE for the allowance guard
@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers for integration tests
better-sqlite3 as a test harness
events.decision_reason: A conditional UPDATE inside a D1 batch cannot abort the batch — it silently reports zero changes after the inserts have already committed, which would admit an event without reserving its allowance. The NOT NULL violation is the only mechanism that rolls the whole batch back. vitest-pool-workers 0.9.14 fails to start against the hoisted miniflare; Node 22's built-in node:sqlite gave the same SQLite engine with no new dependency.
test_evidence_refs: 205 cases across API-, AUTH- and PERSIST- ranges, all passing
events.limitations: The SQLite harness exercises real SQL, real transactions and the real idempotency guards, but not Cloudflare network behaviour, D1 replicas or true OS-level parallelism.
events.next_step: Six security findings from A10 to fix.

events.goal: Challenge the implementation independently rather than confirm it.
events.decision_summary: 40+ threats with honest per-control status, 30 blocking acceptance checks, 9 explicitly accepted risks, and 156 security cases of which 6 are asserted failures against real findings.
events.decision_reason: A finding is only real when a test fails on it. The critical finding: openCredential accepted an optional expected AAD, so a lookup by connection id would decrypt any tenant's row because the stored AAD travels with the row and satisfies the GCM tag.
test_evidence_refs: 156 security cases, 150 passing, 6 failing by design
A10's independently written Stripe and Svix verifiers proved byte-compatible with A02's
events.limitations: Two independent readings of a specification agreeing is the strongest evidence available without a live provider call. It is not a live provider call.

events.goal: Make the 500-case release gate honest rather than inflated.
events.decision_summary: 578 designed cases across 12 categories, every category above its minimum, plus a checker that fails on duplicate ids, shortfalls, missing fields and identical requirement+setup pairs.
alternatives_considered: Renumbering the 449 already-implemented case ids onto the ledger
events.decision_reason: Padding detection matters more than the total. The checker was smoke-tested by deliberately corrupting a copy of the ledger; every detector produced its own specific failure.
test_evidence_refs: node scripts/verify-test-cases.mjs exits 0; --strict blocks on reconciliation
events.limitations: The ledger is a design, and 415 of its cases are not yet implemented. Implemented ids and ledger ids are currently separate namespaces; the ledger must be reconciled to reality before the gate can be claimed.

events.goal: Mount the routers behind a strict Content-Security-Policy and confirm the deployed pages are correct by looking at them.
events.decision_summary: Hash-based CSP with no unsafe-inline, computed from the same constants the page renders. One narrow concession: style-src-attr allows inline style attributes; script-src-attr is none.
alternatives_considered: Nonce-based CSP
A blanket unsafe-inline
Leaving inline geometry blocked
events.decision_reason: The first strict policy blocked inline style attributes, so the demo page verification-rate meter fell back to full width: the number said 33% and the bar said 100%. The markup was correct throughout — only a screenshot revealed it. On a product whose thesis is that a partial result must never display as a pass, an inflated bar is the worst available defect, so the concession was taken deliberately and named in the code rather than hidden. A blanket unsafe-inline would not even have worked, since the spec ignores it while a hash is present.
test_evidence_refs: Deployed to staging and screenshotted before and after; meter renders 33% after the fix
All 13 public routes return 200 with the policy applied
events.limitations: The concession stays until the computed geometry moves to predefined classes. Responsive widths were not confirmed through this tool and are covered by the browser suite instead.
events.next_step: Remove style-src-attr once A05 converts the geometry to classes.

events.goal: Replace the holding page at verify.itisyou.app with the real public site.
events.decision_summary: Deployed the marketing site, the worked-example demo, the legal pages and the development story to production. The customer application is reachable but runs on a synthetic data port, labelled as such on every page.
alternatives_considered: Wait until the real data layer is wired before deploying anything
events.decision_reason: A holding page tells a visitor nothing. The public pages are complete and every claim on them maps to implemented behaviour, and the synthetic customer pages carry an unmissable banner plus a stripe. Shipping honest incompleteness is better than shipping nothing, and it makes the work inspectable.
test_evidence_refs: All 11 production routes return 200
CSP and HSTS present on production responses
Bundle scanned for secrets before upload: clean
events.limitations: Nothing is for sale. No account can be created. Every page under /app returns synthetic data and says so. Live payments and provider-backed evidence both await owner credentials.
events.next_step: Wire the real D1 repositories behind the three data ports.

events.goal: Stop the tenant-scope source scan reporting customer-facing prose as unscoped SQL.
events.decision_summary: The SQL detector now requires a verb AND a clause, both uppercase, and a paired check fails the build on any lowercase SQL verb in the data layer.
alternatives_considered: Add an allowlist entry for the offending file
Reword the customer-facing copy to avoid the word update
events.decision_reason: The payment-recovery notice says you can update your card and mentions runs and evidence, which a case-insensitive keyword match read as an unscoped query on customer tables. Allowlisting the file or bending the copy around a detector both leave the detector wrong. A security check that fires on English gets muted, and a muted check protects nothing. Tightening to uppercase opens a loophole for lowercase SQL, so the two changes are a pair and neither is safe alone.
test_evidence_refs: Measured rather than assumed: across 285 string literals in the data layer the old rule detected 121 statements and the new rule detects exactly the same 121 — zero detection lost
SEC-205 added; 19 cases in the file pass
events.limitations: The scan is a structural heuristic over source text. It cannot see SQL assembled at runtime, and it is not a substitute for the behavioural tenant-isolation tests.

events.goal: Make every outward-facing statement true today rather than true when finished, and close any purchase or activation path resting on something that is not.
events.decision_summary: Twelve published claims were corrected against what the code does today. The site had been promising a second coverage mode that would detect a run that never started; nothing implements it, the onboarding form still offered it, and the development story already claimed that had been fixed. The connector claim — we read the record back from HubSpot and Resend — is now accompanied on every page that makes it by the statement that it has never been run against a real provider account. The seven-day payment-recovery policy is now displayed on the one page a prospective customer can actually read. Eleven regression cases (CUST-330..CUST-340) drive the real Worker entry point and assert the response body. A second pass, prompted by a design audit of a Stitch-generated landing page that carried two false compliance-certification badges, a fabricated attributed quote, auto-remediation language and USD pricing tiers, ruled each of those classes out on the real site. Three were absent outright. One heading on the visual development story read "Independently audited" — an internal cross-review, but in the exact register of a security attestation — and was reworded. Four figures were retyped as literals where a constant governs them and now interpolate it.
alternatives_considered: Soften the development story so the coverage-mode claim became true by wording rather than by code
Add the provider-proof caveat once in the footer instead of beside each claim it qualifies
Take the pricing page down entirely rather than disclose terms nobody can buy
Assert the corrected copy by rendering the page functions directly, as the existing suite does
Report the four absent claim classes as a prose negative without a test, since nothing was found
events.decision_reason: The coverage-mode claim was fixed in code rather than in prose because the story was describing a real fix that had not been made, and rewriting the description of a fix is how a project learns to describe instead of fix. The provider-proof notice sits against each claim rather than in the footer because a caveat a reader meets after forming the belief has not corrected anything. The pricing page stays because the purchase control was already visibly closed and the terms are what a buyer needs to evaluate the product at all. The tests go through apps/app/src/index.ts because the dominant defect on this project is correct code reached by nothing: a case that calls PricingPage() proves the function is right and proves nothing about what GET /pricing puts on the wire. The four absent claim classes got regression cases anyway, because "we looked and found nothing" is worth nothing once the looking stops: a negative finding without a standing check is a statement about one afternoon. The retyped figures got a source-level assertion rather than a rendering one, because four copies of "30 days" all render correctly right up to the moment the constant changes, which is exactly when a claims test should fire and a rendering assertion would not.
test_evidence_refs: tests/integration/public/claims.test.ts — 11 cases, all committed red against the site as it stood (11 failed) and green after the corrections (11 passed)
CUST-334 asserts the payment-recovery disclosure against PAYMENT_RECOVERY_POLICY itself, so changing the approved window fails the test rather than leaving stale prose
CUST-331 sweeps all ten public pages for the withdrawn coverage promise rather than checking the two that were reported
tests/unit/ui/pages.test.ts CUST-043 tightened to the unqualified heading, so restoring the old copy fails in two places

CUST-342..345 assert the four audited claim classes absent from every public page, matching visible text and raw markup; CUST-342 was red on the "Independently audited" heading and is green after the rewording
CUST-346 asserts price, currency, allowance, retention and recovery window against LIMITS and PAYMENT_RECOVERY_POLICY, and that no $, EUR or USD figure appears on any page

CUST-347 reads the six customer-facing copy modules as source and fails on a hard-coded governed figure; proven red against the HEAD blobs, which carried four (two in faq.ts, one in legal.ts, one in the /pricing meta description)

No element and no 
 or  block exists on any public page — asserted, not assumed, so no badge graphic or install command can appear without failing a test
events.limitations: The onboarding coverage-mode selector is asserted by the domain constant it now reads, not by an HTTP request: every /app route answers 401 without a session, and seeding one needs a real D1 and the owner-authentication wiring. Four claims are recommended for removal rather than qualification (docs/product-scope.md 11.3) and were deliberately left in place, because removing a page or a policy is the owner’s decision. No provider was contacted and no credential exists, so the mock-only statement is itself the only thing that could be verified about the connectors. CUST-343, CUST-344 and CUST-345 were green from the moment they were written: nothing was found for those three classes, and they are standing guards rather than regressions. The competitor check bars a capability claim about a named competitor, not the naming itself — "we never see inside n8n, Make, Zapier" is deliberately still permitted, because it is a statement about our own blindness.
events.next_step: Owner to rule on the four removal candidates in docs/product-scope.md 11.3. The provider-proof notice comes down when CONN-900 and CONN-901 have actually run against real accounts, and the activation notice when the event-intake route, the Resend webhook mount, the entitlement check and the billing maintenance pass are all wired.

events.goal: Make POST /api/v1/events reachable, since the route the product is named for answered 404 in every deployment.
events.decision_summary: Mounted the events route and moved its two D1 ports from the test tree into apps/app/src/db/, where SEC-201 requires SQL to live. They had been written in tests because their author did not own that directory, which meant production implemented the port nowhere at all.
alternatives_considered: Leave the ports in the test tree and import them from production. Rejected: it would make a test file a production dependency and invert the dependency the lint rule exists to protect.
events.decision_reason: A module that is mounted nowhere is not a feature. The schema had carried signing_key_hash and signing_key_ref since migration 0001 and setSigningKey had existed to write them, but nothing ever called it, so no customer could hold a key and no signed request could be verified. The intake was missing one layer below where anyone was looking.
test_evidence_refs: live probe: POST /api/v1/events returned 404 before the mount and 401 SIGNATURE_INVALID after
tsc exit 0
events.limitations: Proven against a local worker only. Not yet reproduced against a candidate deployment, and EVENT_SIGNING_ROOT_KEY is not provisioned in any environment, so a genuinely signed event has never been admitted anywhere. The 503-not-401 behaviour when the key id is real but the root key is missing is UNVERIFIED.
events.next_step: Auditor reproduces against a candidate release; owner provisions EVENT_SIGNING_ROOT_KEY.

events.goal: Correct a causal claim I published in commit 66b8d38 that turned out to be false.
events.decision_summary: Commit 66b8d38 states that the test runner instability is caused by our own agent concurrency. That is wrong. Two specialists independently established the real cause: SEC-632 blocks its worker event loop for 218,015 ms inside a synchronous execFileSync, against a next-slowest file of 2,188 ms, and the framework birpc timer is a hard-coded 60 s. One file, one worker, an otherwise empty pool reproduces it.
alternatives_considered: Lower maxWorkers, which appeared to help intermittently and would have treated a symptom. Raise the RPC timeout, which is not configurable in either installed version and would have hidden the defect rather than fixed it.
events.decision_reason: The apparent failures moved between files across runs because they were whichever files shared a worker with the blocking one. That pattern is what made concurrency a plausible cause, and it is exactly why a plausible cause needed an experiment rather than an explanation. Git history cannot be rewritten on this project, so the earlier claim is corrected here rather than erased.
test_evidence_refs: isolation run: one file, one worker, empty pool, timeout still fires
measured 218,015 ms for secret-hygiene.test.ts against 2,188 ms next slowest
diff of createForksRpcOptions across both installed versions: no timeout key in either
events.limitations: A second isolation pass to confirm SEC-632 is the ONLY contributor did not finish before the session limit terminated it. Until it does, one cause is established and a second is not ruled out.
events.next_step: A09 fixes SEC-632 at source; two consecutive clean full runs close it.

events.goal: Stop an unearned claim reaching a visitor, after a design tool proved that instructing it is not a control.
events.decision_summary: Added a claim scanner and wired it into the release gate. Sixteen screens were generated in Google Stitch; halfway through, the tool was given an explicit itemised instruction to stop making unearned claims and visibly adopted it, restating the rules back. The finished export still carried absolutist security vocabulary on 13 of 20 screens, a compliance badge we do not hold on 6, a second one on 2, a fabricated quote naming two real competitors on 4, and AUTO-REMEDIAT on 2.
alternatives_considered: Rely on review. Rejected on the evidence above: correcting a generator does not clean what it already produced and does not reliably stop it producing more.
events.decision_reason: The first version of the scanner reported 96 findings and almost none were claims: it flagged the constant that defines the forbidden phrases, the tests asserting the validator rejects them, and the audit report whose finding was that none of it appears on the site. A check with that signal-to-noise is switched off within a week. Narrowing it to source that renders to a visitor, plus the rendered HTML itself, took it to 3 — all denials, each carrying a stated reason.
test_evidence_refs: scan-claims exit 0 on the tree
scan-claims exit 1 on a planted certification / remediation / social-proof claim, then 0 again after restore
rendered pass over 21 served pages: exit 0
events.limitations: It proves no banned phrase is present. It does not prove the remaining claims are true; only checking each against the code does that. The rendered pass is only as current as the pages fed to it.
events.next_step: Run the served-pages pass against the candidate deployment on every release.

events.goal: Reproduce six claims other specialists and the lead had closed, by issuing real requests against a candidate and reading the resulting state.
events.decision_summary: The auditor closed one open question and opened seven findings. It established what the lead had not: with a REAL signing key id present and EVENT_SIGNING_ROOT_KEY absent, the intake answers 503 SIGNING_KEY_UNREADABLE rather than 401 — the fault is ours and the status says so. It also refused to verify notifications, because doing so required inventing a Stripe webhook secret, and a green result under a fabricated credential is indistinguishable in a register from a real one.
alternatives_considered: Accept the lead's own demonstration of the lead's own claim scanner. Rejected: the auditor defeated that gate in one attempt with plain English.
events.decision_reason: Three findings landed on the lead. The claim scanner passed "we fix your broken automation for you" and "we guarantee 100% accuracy" while catching "guaranteed accuracy" — it turned on a verb ending, so it certified the page it was meant to guard. The gap register cited the development story as evidence for backup restoration, and the story contains no such event; the citation was false and the row is withdrawn. And the register's owner column named agents that were not on the roster, which is unassigned work wearing owner labels.
test_evidence_refs: 503 SIGNING_KEY_UNREADABLE reproduced with a seeded workflow and no root key
12 further denial legs: wrong workflow 403, stale/future timestamp 401, stale occurred_at 422, bad schema 422, 64KiB 413
scan-claims now exits 1 on all three phrases that previously passed
HEAD moved four times during the pass: 5b7c450 to 25a41fc to 4b27b01 to 0c7fc08
events.limitations: Nothing in this pass is deployment-verified; every measurement is local. There is no frozen candidate — HEAD moved four times while the audit ran, and one request returned 503 worker restarted mid-request. The auditor's own could-not-verify list has eight entries.
events.next_step: Freeze a candidate commit before the next audit pass. Notifications stay unverified until a real Stripe webhook secret exists.
